agree.reason: The letter is candid and gives two concrete business reasons plus a commuting subsidy and long notice, but a remote hire weighing whether to leave gets no six-month review, no sign the partners will listen, and a flat 'no other exceptions', so many will comply grudgingly and some will look elsewhere.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief, but 'they could see we didn't' and the claim that the 30% delay comes from screen-based learning go a little beyond what the clients and the review records actually show.

works_the_facts.reason: The 30% figure and the lost bids are stated as given and never worked further: there is no translation into time or careers, and the letter leaves out that 5 of 6 project leads are already in three days a week, which is the strongest fact for the mentoring argument.

right_comparison.reason: The letter never describes what happens if fully remote work continues (more lost final interviews, a widening gap for juniors), so the status quo is only implied through last year's losses.

qualification.reason: The writer had a six-month review to offer and left it out, so the policy reads as permanent and unconditional, with no checkable date or measure that could change it.

objections.reason: It acknowledges that the 15 remote hires are having their terms changed and gives notice and a commuting subsidy, but it skips the strongest reassurance available (the six-month review) and never addresses why three days rather than fewer.

fit.reason: It is a one-page email with a clear subject line, a bulleted list of practical details and the Friday 10 a.m. meeting with a contact route, which is exactly what was asked.
